body:
PurRDF adoption and grounded preferred-provider enforcement in #53 are now the highest-priority delivery path. Source review found that completing all of #43 and #44 is not a prerequisite for a useful locked dependency/source/symbol foundation here: the existing shared resolver and verified Tree boundary already support a host-source contract.

The first coherent extraction must bind exact locked package/source identities and eligible aliased dependency edges to supplied verified sources, resolve actual symbols through the shared resolver, and fail actionably on missing, ambiguous or incomplete evidence. A crate-name match or a fixture package named after the provider is insufficient. This does not authorize a parallel resolver or Cargo metadata JSON path.

All original requirements here remain open: declared cfg inputs/results, path and external/std resolution, explicit macro/unsupported markers and differential acceptance. Portability acceptance remains with #43/#44/#46. No implementation or production provider enforcement is claimed by this ordering correction.
